newsitem.title: HUNGARY: TVK 96 profit down, raw material costs up.
newsitem.headline: TVK 96 profit down, raw material costs up.

text.p: Hungarian chemicals maker Tiszai Vegyi Kombinat Rt's (TVK) 1996 net profit dropped to 7.81 billion forints in 1996 from 10.47 billion in 1995, the company said on Friday.
"In 1995 the chemical cycle was at its peak, thus the 1996 foreign currency prices of our main products were lower," TVK said in its earnings report.
At the same time, the average price of TVK's main raw material, chemicals benzene, rose 21 percent to $193 per tonne in 1996.
TVK's total IAS unconsolidated sales rose to 62.09 billion forints in 1996 from 60.67 billion forints in 1995.

Production of all polymers was lower in 1996 than in 1995, with an output of 89,300 tonnes of LDPE (low-density polyethylene) down 15 percent on 1995, 154,400 tonnes of HDPE (high density polyethylene) down eight percent and 135,600 tonnes of granulated PP (polypropylene) down one percent.
Total polymer sales edged up to 42.22 billion forints in 1996 from 41.02 billion in 1995, while export prices dropped 13 percent for LDPE, 14 percent for HDPE and 15 percent for PP.
Domestic polymer prices remained virtually flat in 1996, with a 2.5 drop in PP price and a one percent rise in LDPE price.
The number of employees fell to 3,860 from 4,597 during 1996, but the number of those made redundant was only 220 as 413 were transferred to TVK subsidiaries.

TVK has an issued share capital of 24 billion forints. Its main shareholders are foreign institutional investors holding 51 percent and domestic institutional investors holding 23.44 percent. TVK itself holds 12.53 percent.
On the Budapest Stock Exchange, TVK shares closed at 2,200 forints, down 420.
